# Groups, Slopes & Interactions

Week 6 taught you that a group is just a predictor. Week 8 taught you that a predictor's coefficient depends on what else is in the model. This week those two facts meet in a single regression: one categorical predictor, one continuous predictor, and a question neither week could ask.

The additive model — group plus covariate — draws **parallel lines**: same slope for every group, different heights. That is a strong assumption, and most people never notice they made it. An **interaction** relaxes it, and lets the slope itself differ from group to group.

::: callout-note
## The sentence to watch for this week

Once an interaction is in the model, there is no such thing as "the effect of X." There is only the effect of X **at a particular value of the other variable**. That is why we report simple slopes, and why centering stops being cosmetic.
:::

We work two examples deliberately: one where the interaction is real and changes the story (tutoring helps the students who study least), and one where we test for an interaction, do not find it, and report the additive model like adults. Both are correct outcomes. Only one of them usually gets written up honestly.

::: callout-important
## In-class check today

**In-Class Check 3** runs at the start of class — about 20 minutes, open notes, open readings, open past labs. It covers **Weeks 7 and 8**: R², adjusted R², the residual standard error, the nested *F* test, and interpreting a coefficient with its *holding constant* clause.
:::
